name: Morgen
subcategory: personal tasks, routines and daily planning
tagline: Unify calendars and tasks, create booking pages, and plan work across time zones

pricing.notes: Typical Pro monthly rate; annual billing may be lower.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Morgen, unify calendars and tasks, create booking pages, and plan work across time zones. The hard boundary is multiple calendar providers, task integrations, mobile apps, and sync reliability, plus cross-device reliability and workflow polish.
coreLoopDIY: Unify calendars and tasks, capture and schedule work across time zones from a focused today view, create booking pages, and keep history locally.
whatYouLose: multiple calendar providers, task integrations, mobile apps, and sync reliability
ongoingBurden: recurrence edge cases, notifications, sync conflicts, calendar APIs, mobile capture, and backups
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Morgen because task software is sticky because trust, speed, and ubiquitous capture matter more than the database schema. The recurring cost buys recurrence edge cases, notifications, sync conflicts, calendar APIs, mobile capture, and backups, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Vikunja
priorArt.desc: Mature open-source task and project manager with lists, kanban, and recurring work.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Pro plan and a personal desktop task manager DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Morgen in an empty repository.
Use Tauri 2, React, TypeScript, SQLite, and desktop notifications; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: unify calendars and tasks, capture and schedule work across time zones from a focused today view, create booking pages, and keep history locally.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create inbox, today, upcoming, someday, and completed views with fast keyboard capture.
Support projects, tags, due dates, start dates, priorities, notes, subtasks, and attachments.
Implement robust daily, weekly, monthly, and custom recurring rules with tests.
Add a focus view with one active task, timer, and optional desktop notification.
Provide search, saved filters, undo, and a completed-task archive.
Export and import a documented JSON format and make automatic local backups.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out team assignment and comments.
Deliberately leave out two-way calendar or email synchronization.
Deliberately leave out native mobile apps and cloud accounts.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
